findings.title: 'Lock when I leave the app' (default on) fires for the app's own system pickers: Save-to-device returns to the lock screen and Restore-by-picker can never complete
findings.evidence: Capacitor fires appStateChange(isActive=false) from BridgeActivity.onStop when activityDepth==0 (node_modules/@capacitor/android/capacitor/src/main/java/com/getcapacitor/BridgeActivity.java:113-119); lifecycle.ts:67-78 treats every such event as leave(): onLocked() + control('lockAll') + flushAll, and prefs.ts:22 makes lockOnLeave default true. ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT (DiaryFilesPlugin.java:147-151, startActivityForResult) and the WebView's <input type=file> chooser (BridgeWebChromeClient.showFilePicker -> ACTION_GET_CONTENT) open DocumentsUI, an opaque full-screen activity of another app, so MainActivity reaches onStop while the picker is open and the UI and the core sessions lock. Consequence 1: 'Save to device' writes the file (the blob is already in JS) but the user returns to the lock screen. Consequence 2: RestoreSection.onFileChange (lines 123-131) -> backupApi.inspectFile -> the core answers 423 -> fileError + lock screen; choosing the file again locks again, so restoring through the picker is impossible with the default setting. The owner's test script (docs/ANDROID-PHONE-TEST.he.md part 2, section 1) will hit this.
findings.fix: Suspend the lock (not the flush) while an app-initiated system UI is pending: a suspendLockOnLeave() token set by files.ts around createDocument/share and by the host around the WebView file chooser (or route Restore through the plugin's ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT so one token covers it), honoured by shouldLockOnLeave(); alternatively lock on resume only when no own activity result is pending. Add a lifecycle test for the suspended case.

findings.title: Every resume or start of a LOCKED session cancels all pending reminders (423 treated like 'no session'), and nothing re-plans after unlocking
findings.evidence: notifications.ts:226-235: a rejected loadHabits/loadProgress -> cancelAll() and reason 'failed'. index.ts:177 wires onResume -> scheduler.resync(); with lock-on-leave on, every return to the app happens locked, so habitsApi.list answers 423 (src/api/client.ts:218 throws, reportLocked) and the whole plan is cancelled. The same happens on a cold start of a remembered locked session (useReminders plan() runs with status 'authenticated' while sessionLocked) and after the auto-lock timer. Unlocking (LockScreen.onSubmit -> verifyPassword -> unlock()) triggers no sync: useReminders' effect depends only on [phone, enabled, locale] and the core posts no habits-changed. So in the default configuration the OS-scheduled reminders are wiped each time the user opens the app and come back only after a habit edit/log, a language change or a settings toggle - contradicting WP-8's acceptance ('the reminder fires while the app is closed'). notifications.test.ts:223 enshrines 'cancel when the habits cannot be loaded (no session)' without distinguishing 423.
findings.fix: In run(), keep the existing plan on a load failure (return 'failed' without cancelAll) unless the error is a real 401/no-session; and re-sync after a successful unlock (make useReminders depend on the lock state, or let LockContext.unlock call phone.sync). Add tests: 423 keeps the pending notifications; unlock -> one resync.

findings.title: The required comparison of two biometric plugin candidates is documented nowhere; the plan has no WP-7/8/9 status line
findings.evidence: The package asked to compare 2 maintained biometric plugins (maintenance, Capacitor 8 support, licence) and say why one was chosen. grep for capacitor-native-biometric / capgo / aparajita / biometric-auth in docs/, mobile/plugins/README.md, README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md: no hit. A local plugin (DiaryBiometricPlugin, framework BiometricPrompt + Keystore, no dependency, no network) was written instead - defensible, but the rationale is missing. docs/ANDROID-PLAN.md's status section lists WP-1..6 and WP-14 only (the plan is outside the package's ownership).
findings.fix: Add the comparison and the decision to mobile/plugins/README.md; the main session adds the WP-7/8/9 status line (feature flag BIOMETRIC_UNLOCK_ENABLED=false until the core implements /api/auth/biometric/*).

findings.title: Share: the cache copy is deleted as soon as the chooser returns, not when the receiving app finished reading it
findings.evidence: shareFile deletes the copy in finally right after Share.share resolves; SharePlugin.java:77-93 resolves in the chooser's activityResult, i.e. when the chooser activity finishes (right after the target was chosen), while the target app reads the content:// grant afterwards. A receiver that copies the stream asynchronously (Drive upload, mail attach) can find the file gone. Cannot be demonstrated without a device.
findings.fix: Try 'Share -> Save to Drive' and 'Share -> Gmail' on the phone (part 2, section 1.4 of the Hebrew guide); if it fails, delete the previous copy at the next share / app start instead of immediately.

findings.title: The first VIEW filter matches every application/octet-stream file, not only .mpd
findings.evidence: The filter has schemes content/file and mimeType application/octet-stream with no pathPattern, so 'Your Personal Diary' is offered as 'Open with' for every unknown-type file (.bin, .dat, ...) and the user only learns it is not a backup after the restore card inspects it. It is what the package text literally asked for; the second filter already covers *.mpd by name.
findings.fix: Keep only the pathPattern filter (second one), or add the .mpd pathPatterns to the octet-stream filter as well; verify the 'Open with' list on the phone.
